theme.title: Seventies Finals
theme.subtitle: The NBA, 1975–79
theme.recap: The late 1970s spread titles around: Golden State swept, Boston won a triple-overtime classic and Seattle won its first title.

questions.prompt: How many regular-season games did the 1974–75 Bullets win before the Finals?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Washington Bullets (60–22) for the championship

funFacts.text: The Washington Bullets had only recently relocated from Baltimore, where the franchise previously played.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: having moved from Baltimore prior to the 1973–74 season

funFacts.text: Wes Unseld and Elvin Hayes anchored a team coached by future Celtics icon K. C. Jones.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: led by Wes Unseld and Elvin Hayes, and coached by K. C. Jones

funFacts.text: Washington knocked out the defending champion Celtics on the way to the championship series.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: then overcame the Buffalo Braves and the defending champion Boston Celtics

questions.prompt: Jo Jo White was 1976 Finals MVP. How many total points did he score in the six games?
questions.context: 1976 NBA Finals · six games vs Phoenix

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Jo Jo White scored 15 points, giving him 130 points in six games, and was named the series MVP.

funFacts.text: Boston had dealt Paul Westphal to Phoenix for Charlie Scott before the series, a trade that shaped both teams.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: including trading Westphal to Phoenix for Charlie Scott

funFacts.text: The Celtics faced Cleveland's 'Miracle of Richfield' team before reaching the Finals.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: the "Miracle of Richfield" Cleveland Cavaliers

funFacts.text: The opposing Suns made the championship series despite entering the playoffs from the West's third seed.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: 3 x-Phoenix Suns 42 40 .512

questions.prompt: In the triple-overtime Game 5 of 1976, reserve Glenn McDonald scored how many points?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Glenn McDonald scored eight points in the game, all in overtime.

funFacts.text: Phoenix's Paul Westphal deliberately called a timeout the Suns didn't have to gain a tactical advantage.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The Suns' Paul Westphal also intentionally called a timeout even though his team had no more remaining

funFacts.text: John Havlicek appeared to win the epic with a late basket, only for more time to remain on the clock.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Havlicek hit what appeared to be the game-winning shot at the end of the second overtime

funFacts.text: The dramatic winner came from a lightly used Boston reserve, not one of the celebrated starters.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Glenn McDonald, a little-used Celtic reserve player

questions.prompt: Through the first three games of the 1975 Finals, how many points did Golden State's bench score?
questions.note: 115, to Washington's 53, on the way to a sweep.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: the Warriors' bench players had outscored the Bullets' reserves 115–53

funFacts.text: Golden State had to host part of the Finals at the Cow Palace because the Ice Follies occupied its arena.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: the Oakland facility being unavailable due to the Ice Follies

funFacts.text: Jamaal Wilkes's defense against Elvin Hayes helped neutralize Washington's frontcourt advantage.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: the defensive play of the seemingly undersized Jamaal Wilkes on Bullets' power forward Elvin Hayes

funFacts.text: Backup center George Johnson provided timely scoring and rebounding during the Warriors' surprise sweep.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: backup center George Johnson had 10 points and nine rebounds off the bench

questions.prompt: Seattle won the 1979 title. What did its top scorer, Gus Williams, average in the Finals?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Gus Williams of the SuperSonics was the top scorer, averaging 28.6 points per game

funFacts.text: Dennis Johnson, not Williams, won Finals MVP for the SuperSonics' title run.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Dennis Johnson of the SuperSonics was named as the NBA Finals MVP

funFacts.text: Seattle's triumph avenged a Finals defeat to the same Washington Bullets team the previous year.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The series was a rematch of the previous year's NBA Finals, which the Bullets won

funFacts.text: Before the SuperSonics won, Seattle's last men's major professional sports title came in ice hockey.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Seattle Metropolitans' victory in the 1917 Stanley Cup Final
